novelty_basis: Searches (2026-10-18) on CA prediction complexity, branching-program/light-cone complexity and computational irreducibility (Wolfram; Israeli-Goldenfeld, arXiv:nlin/0309047; Moore's prediction papers) found no notion of streaming width of t-step rules and no analysis of this rule; the burn-time mechanism itself is elementary. Small.
proof_check: written proof (proofs/paper/C15.md Theorem 4); fast-forward agrees with direct simulation on 27,000 (row, t) pairs during development and in all EXP-C15-03 cases; widths and the lower-bound residual family checked to t = 12 (EXP-C15-05); awaiting independent skeptic review
statement:
For the fuse magma [[0,0,0],[0,0,1],[1,2,2]] (0 burnt, 1 burning, 2 intact): burn times satisfy tau_i = 0 (x_i = 0),
tau_(i+1) + 2 (x_i = 2), tau_(i+1) (x_i = 1, x_(i+1) = 2), 1 (x_i = 1, x_(i+1) != 2); the row at any time t is
obtained from them in O(L) operations; and floor((m+1)/2) <= lambda(t) <= 3t + 3 with m = floor(t/2), so the
streaming width grows linearly (computed lambda(t) = t + 2 for t <= 12).
title: The fuse magma: linear streaming width, yet an O(L) fast-forward for every t
